source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A child on stimulant therapy should have which monitored for growth suppression?
questions.rationale: Stimulants can suppress growth, so weight and height are monitored.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Stimulants (PDF p. 251)
questions.quote: Growth suppression: Monitor thechild's weight and height

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client on disulfiram should avoid which product?
questions.rationale: Products such as aftershave, cologne, mouthwash, and some cough syrups contain alcohol and can trigger a reaction.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Disulfiram (PDF p. 251)
questions.quote: Aftershave lotion

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Disulfiram is best suited for which client?
questions.rationale: Disulfiram is useful for persons motivated to abstain who are not impulsive.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Disulfiram (PDF p. 251)
questions.quote: Usefulfor persons who are motivated to abstain from drinking and who are not impulsive.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Why is atropine given before ECT?
questions.rationale: Atropine decreases secretions; succinylcholine relaxes muscles; methohexital is the anesthetic.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, ECT (PDF p. 252)
questions.quote: Atropine sulfate To decrease secretions

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which is a common short-term effect after ECT?
questions.rationale: Clients may be confused and have short-term memory impairment; reorient them.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, ECT (PDF p. 252)
questions.quote: Following ECT the client may be mildly confused, disoriented and may have short term memory impa

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: What preparation is needed before ECT?
questions.rationale: NPO after midnight, void, IV access, and informed consent.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, ECT (PDF p. 251)
questions.quote: NPO after midnight

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Per the handout, how many ECT treatments usually produce a therapeutic effect?
questions.rationale: Usually 6–12 treatments (up to 15), spaced about 48 hours apart.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, ECT (PDF p. 252)
questions.quote: 6 -12 treatments(up to 15)

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: A woman who never wanted children becomes an over-involved 'super-mom.' Which defense?
questions.rationale: Reaction formation is acting opposite to one's true feelings.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Defense Mechanisms (PDF p. 253)
questions.quote: Acting the opposite of what one thinks are feels.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: A man angry at his boss yells at his wife. Which defense?
questions.rationale: Displacement vents feelings on a less threatening person.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Defense Mechanisms (PDF p. 253)
questions.quote: A person who is mad at the boss yells at his or her spouse

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: What distinguishes suppression from repression?
questions.rationale: Suppression is conscious exclusion; repression is unconscious forgetting.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Defense Mechanisms (PDF p. 253)
questions.quote: Conscious forgetting

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: A teen tempted by friends develops sudden blindness without concern. Which defense?
questions.rationale: Conversion expresses emotional conflict as a sensorimotor symptom, often with indifference.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Defense Mechanisms (PDF p. 253)
questions.quote: Expression of an emotional conflict through the development of a physical symptom

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: Which personality component seeks instant gratification?
questions.rationale: The id seeks instant gratification; the superego is conscience; the ego mediates.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Personality Structure (PDF p. 252)
questions.quote: Seeks instant gratification

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: An adult remembering childhood events with effort uses which level of awareness?
questions.rationale: Preconscious material can be recalled with effort.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Levels of Awareness (PDF p. 254)
questions.quote: Not currently in the person's awareness, but he or she can recall them with some effort.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: Remotivation therapy is unsuitable for which client?
questions.rationale: Remotivation discusses neutral topics for rehabilitative clients, not actively psychotic ones.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Psychotherapeutic Interventions (PDF p. 254)
questions.quote: not for activetly psychotic patients

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: What is the ideal size of a therapy group?
questions.rationale: Minimum 3 members; ideal 8–10.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Group Therapy (PDF p. 254)
questions.quote: Minimum number of members in a group is 3, while the ideal number is 8 —10

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: Dolls are used to help an abused child express feelings. This is:
questions.rationale: Play therapy lets the child experience intense emotion safely through play.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Play Therapy (PDF p. 254)
questions.quote: For victims of child abuse, give dolls.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: Which therapy uses free association and dream analysis?
questions.rationale: Psychoanalysis explores the unconscious using free association and dream analysis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Psychoanalysis (PDF p. 254)
questions.quote: Utilizes dream analysis and free association

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: How long does a crisis state usually last?
questions.rationale: A crisis is self-limiting, usually lasting 4–6 weeks.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Crisis (PDF p. 255)
questions.quote: Lasts for 4 — 6 weeks

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Losing a job suddenly is which type of crisis?
questions.rationale: Situational crises are unexpected external events like job loss or death.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Crisis (PDF p. 255)
questions.quote: Loss of a job

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A community hit by a typhoon experiences which crisis type?
questions.rationale: Adventitious crises include natural disasters, war, and violent crimes.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Crisis (PDF p. 255)
questions.quote: Includes natural disasters and acts 0 nature like

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: What is the nurse's role during crisis intervention?
questions.rationale: The nurse is active and directive in crisis intervention.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Crisis Intervention (PDF p. 256)
questions.quote: Active and directive, the nurse has to assist the patient

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which Philippine law defines and penalizes rape?
questions.rationale: RA 8353 (Anti-Rape Law of 1997) defines rape; RA 9262 is anti-VAWC; RA 7610 child abuse; RA 9165 dangerous drugs.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Rape (PDF p. 256)
questions.quote: According to Republic Act 8353

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: How should the nurse support a rape survivor in the ER?
questions.rationale: Provide emotional support, let her set the pace, and give back control; filing charges is her decision.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Care for Rape Victims (PDF p. 256)
questions.quote: Give as much control back to the victim as possible

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: What is the main problem in autism spectrum disorder?
questions.rationale: ASD involves impaired social interaction and communication with stereotyped behaviors.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Autism (PDF p. 257)
questions.quote: Main Problem: Impaired Interpersonal Functioning

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A child with autism head-bangs during tantrums. What is the priority?
questions.rationale: Safety is priority: helmet, padded walls.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Autism (PDF p. 257)
questions.quote: Helmet
